items_missed: No 'How are you today?' and no agenda statement — never framed what the call would cover or how long it would take, and never asked 'sound good?'
No 'pricing is super simple' opener — went straight into 'on a granular level'
No Worries Damage Coverage never explained — only said the rate 'covers the insurance that we placed on your move,' no $2,000 figure, no 60 cents/lb baseline
Meet Your Mover never mentioned — closest he got was saying the movers would call with an ETA on move day
No special-considerations probe (long walks, narrow hallways, tight turns) despite a 2,500 sq ft two-story origin and an indoor storage unit
Never said the clock starts on-site when the contract opens
Stairs never explained as a time variable, even after capturing 31 boxes upstairs at origin and one piece going upstairs at the destination
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped — with roughly 80 bankers boxes and a 1:30 PM start, consolidation and carload tips were the highest-value thing he could have given
No 'any other questions before I let you go?' close — the customer had to volunteer the who-do-we-call question
top_strength: Genuinely transparent about the afternoon arrival window — he volunteered unprompted that a 1:30 start means a 12:30-2:30 window, explained why the morning slot is held open, and then said outright that if they run past the extra hour Einstein starts discounting. Then he adjusted the start time to fit what the customer actually wanted rather than defending the original slot.
coaching_note: Erik ran a clean intake and a well-built estimate but left the two biggest value plays on the table: he priced the insurance without ever explaining No Worries ($2,000 coverage vs. the 60 cents/lb state baseline), and he skipped Save Your Ass entirely on an 80-box move. Add both and this call clears mastery.
phone_presence_notes: Used 'Mister James' naturally throughout, stayed patient through a scattered customer counting boxes out loud, and turned the rate-increase complaint into real rapport by joking about his own $60/hour starting days.
